memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them.
And I will gain glory through Pharaoh and all his army, through his chariots and
his horsemen. The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I gain glory
through Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen." - Ex 14:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three times in two verses God speaks of gaining glory. It can sound
uncomfortable to modern ears, as though God were seeking applause.

But consider what glory means here. God gaining glory means God being known as
He truly is. Egypt had spent generations bowing to gods that could not save. The
Red Sea would settle the question of who is actually God.

And notice who benefits when God is known truly. Israel gains a Deliverer they
can trust for the next forty years. The nations around them hear and tremble
(Josh 2:10). Even Egypt is told the truth about reality.

It is only harmful when a person seeks glory that does not belong to them.
For God to make Himself known is simply for the truth to be told. Anything less
would be God concealing the most important fact in the universe.

Isaiah 42:8 says, "I am the LORD; that is my name! I will not yield my glory to
another." That is not vanity. It is God refusing to let people build their lives
on a lie.

When God acts for His glory, He is acting for our good, because our good is
found in knowing Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of God's glory as competing with your good, or securing it?
2. Where in your life would you rather have credit than see God known?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, be known through my life. I would rather You receive glory than that I
receive credit. Amen.
